scopes.label: Language platform
scopes.description: Write portable, typed programs with a practical standard foundation.

scopes.label: Application stack
scopes.description: Build backend, browser, data, and background-work applications.

scopes.label: Daily workflow
scopes.description: Edit, test, ship, diagnose, and maintain real TypeRB projects.

areas.title: Language and type system
areas.description: Portable semantics shared by Go, Ruby, TypeScript, and the evaluator.

items.title: Functions, closures, and structured collection blocks
items.description: Use typed function values, lexical capture, and multi-statement map, select, reduce, predicate, and sort-key blocks.

items.title: Records, enums, payload enums, and pattern matching
items.description: Model product and sum types with checked construction, exhaustive cases, raw values, and payload binding.

items.title: Classes, modules, and interfaces
items.description: The object model is usable, while superclass construction, override rules, initialization order, and some generic member semantics remain incomplete.

items.title: Generics and type inference
items.description: Generic aliases, records, enums, classes, functions, and instance methods exist; broader call-site inference and generic member forms remain.

items.title: Union, nullable, and discriminant narrowing
items.description: Normalized unions, nullable narrowing, literal types, and readonly discriminants exist, but structured and collection alternatives need broader flow analysis.

items.title: Result propagation and recovery
items.description: Represent recoverable failures with Result and use prefix try and postfix catch across functions, callbacks, and application packages.

items.title: Aliases and nominal newtypes
items.description: Choose transparent aliases for shorthand and nominal newtypes for distinct represented values, including typed serialization boundaries.

items.title: Checked numeric and value-type semantics
items.description: Integer and Float behavior is portable and checked, while exact large integers, decimal values, rounding, and richer validated value objects remain.

items.title: Mutation, suspension, and structured concurrency effects
items.description: Immutable parameters, explicit local mutation, hidden suspension propagation, cancellation, and bounded concurrent_map exist; general mutation and composition effects remain.

items.title: Tuples, destructuring, and typed projection
items.description: Add position-typed local products, destructured returns, and precise projection without replacing named records at public boundaries.

items.title: Module visibility, initialization, and minimal runtime type information
items.description: Complete public and file-local visibility, cross-file initialization, constant rules, and only the runtime type information justified by real workflows.

areas.title: Compiler and projects
areas.description: The shared compiler pipeline, project model, diagnostics, and development iteration.

items.title: Shared parser, checker, formatter, and typed IR
items.description: Use one compiler-owned grammar and semantic pipeline for formatting, checking, generation, the language server, and the evaluator.

items.title: Go, Ruby, and TypeScript generation
items.description: Generate all three target modes from the same checked TypeRB program while keeping target-only APIs behind explicit platform imports.

items.title: Configured projects and file-root workflows
items.description: Discover trbconfig.jsonc projects or check, build, run, format, lint, and serve an explicit standalone source closure.

items.title: Deterministic diagnostics, linting, and safe fixes
items.description: Structured diagnostics, suggestions, and a small built-in lint registry exist; the stable catalog and bounded third-party rule boundary need broader evidence.

items.title: Incremental analysis and persistent build caching
items.description: Dependency-aware analysis and reusable compiler services exist, while phase-level invalidation, multi-file change sets, and persistent output caches remain.

items.title: TypeRB source maps, stack traces, and debugging
items.description: Generated ranges and Go debug artifacts map back to TypeRB; Ruby and TypeScript source maps, runtime failures, coverage, and complete stack traces remain.

items.title: Workspace graph and coordinated development server
items.description: Coordinate multiple applications and packages with affected builds, watch mode, process readiness, browser bundling, restart, and HMR where ordinary tools are insufficient.

items.title: Read-only compiler tooling protocol
items.description: A versioned project snapshot exposes sources, modules, checked declarations, semantic types, and diagnostics; persistent queries and a stable SDK remain deferred.

items.title: Cross-backend conformance, reliability, and performance
items.description: A large shared test suite exercises the modes, but 1.0 still needs explicit end-to-end conformance, performance baselines, and supported-toolchain reliability gates.

areas.title: Standard library and foundations
areas.description: Portable everyday APIs with the same types, failures, and resource behavior in every mode.

items.title: Scalars, Unicode text, Arrays, Hashes, Range, and iteration
items.description: The daily core is substantial, while Unicode normalization, additional collection aggregation, and a few common structures and text operations remain.

items.title: Bytes, binary encoding, hashing, and secure randomness
items.description: Use Bytes, hex and Base64, modern and compatibility digests, HMAC, constant-time comparison, and secure random generation portably.

items.title: JSON, JSONC, and typed codecs
items.description: Parse general JSON values and encode or decode typed records, enums, newtypes, collections, and standard values with structured errors.

items.title: Date, time, duration, and time zones
items.description: Civil and exact time values, durations, named zones, parsing, formatting, and codecs exist; calendar periods, injectable clocks, and locale formatting remain.

items.title: Filesystem, logical paths, and process access
items.description: Scoped whole-file operations, bounded reads, entries, environment access, and shell-free processes exist; metadata, temporary files, atomic replacement, and streaming remain.

items.title: Full URL, regular expression, and UUID values
items.description: Add strict cross-backend URL parsing and resolution, a portable regular-expression subset, and canonical UUID parsing and generation.

items.title: Streams, buffers, and scoped resource ownership
items.description: Define bounded-memory byte sources and sinks, partial reads, cancellation, and reliable close semantics from concrete file and network workflows.

items.title: CSV, compression, archives, MIME, and multipart data
items.description: Process common structured and binary formats with explicit limits, encoding policy, safe archive paths, and streaming where input can be large.

items.title: Additional collections and exact numeric values
items.description: Add evidence-backed Set and queue structures, aggregation operations, BigInteger, and Decimal without changing current Integer or Float semantics.

items.title: Structured logging, metrics, and tracing foundations
items.description: Web request JSONL logging exists; 1.0 needs application-wide levels, fields, redaction, context propagation, metrics, spans, and replaceable sinks.

items.title: Typed configuration, internationalization, and locale services
items.description: Provide typed startup configuration and evidence-backed message, pluralization, number, currency, date, and locale facilities without exposing secrets.

areas.title: Packages and native interoperability
areas.description: Reproducible TypeRB packages and explicit, typed boundaries to existing ecosystems.

items.title: Distributed package resolution and canonical identity
items.description: Resolve TypeRB source from Git or local paths with canonical manifests, scoped dependency aliases, and one checked package graph.

items.title: Lockfile, checksums, offline, and frozen installation
items.description: Pin commits and content hashes, verify cached source, and install deterministically without network access or lockfile drift.

items.title: Selective updates and semantic version selection
items.description: Selected direct dependency graphs can update while others remain pinned; semantic version constraints, solver policy, and compatibility guidance remain.

items.title: Per-mode native dependency integration
items.description: Merge package-owned Go modules, gems, npm packages, and Bun packages into generated target manifests without changing portable imports.

items.title: TypeScript declaration indexing and adapters
items.description: Index installed declarations and apply package-owned generic, class, interface, component, alias, and Result bridge corrections; broader native shapes remain.

items.title: Ruby and Go native declaration import
items.description: Import ordinary public types from RBS-compatible metadata and Go type information while diagnosing unsupported shapes instead of producing Any.

items.title: Package-owned runtime adapters
items.description: A narrow String-to-String leaf ABI with Result and suspension propagation works in all modes; typed wire values, handles, streams, and lifecycle hooks remain.

items.title: Declarative project input and generated-source protocols
items.description: Versioned declaration, project input, generated source, and call-specialization boundaries support bundled packages; external stability and incremental behavior remain.

items.title: Package author tooling and sandboxed providers
items.description: Authors can validate and run explicit conformance projects; scaffold, inspection, capability permissions, and resource-bounded provider execution remain.

items.title: Publishing, provenance, audit, and namespace-stable APIs
items.description: Complete package publication, signatures, advisories, vulnerability checks, stable cross-package type identity, and production cache policy.

areas.title: Application platform
areas.description: Official and ecosystem capabilities for full-stack services, tools, data, and browser applications.

items.title: Typed command-line applications
items.description: Generate help, conversion, defaults, subcommands, and a Go single binary from records and payload enums; validation, aliases, completion, and more deployment profiles remain.

items.title: Portable Web routing, middleware, and server lifecycle
items.description: File routes, middleware, cookies, CORS, security headers, compression, timeouts, cancellation, graceful shutdown, and in-process testing work across the modes; production hardening remains.

items.title: Typed HTTP path, query, body, and JSON responses
items.description: Bind route parameters, query values, and JSON bodies to checked records and return typed JSON through one portable dispatcher contract.

items.title: Endpoint catalog, OpenAPI, and generated browser clients
items.description: Versioned endpoint metadata, OpenAPI 3.1 output, and a generated TypeScript-browser client exist; validation policy, compatibility checks, and richer wire metadata remain.

items.title: Authentication, authorization, and server sessions
items.description: Portable OIDC bearer validation and typed principals exist; authorization policy, browser login, rotating cookies, CSRF, session storage, and token lifecycle remain.

items.title: Portable outbound HTTP
items.description: Shared HTTP values and a typed browser client exist; Go, Ruby, and server-TypeScript transport, retry, streaming, close, interception, and test doubles remain.

items.title: ORM models, queries, writes, relations, and transactions
items.description: Typed models, associations, preload, locks, batches, writes, transactions, enums, time, and three database systems work across three modes; advanced queries and production policy remain.

items.title: Database schema workflow
items.description: Plan, apply, export, lock, and check schemas with explicit destructive changes; online compatibility, multi-database workflows, fixtures, and release validation remain.

items.title: Background Jobs, schedules, retries, and recovery
items.description: Typed jobs, SQL queues, scheduling, retry, heartbeat, stale recovery, operations commands, and graceful stop work across supported modes and databases; adapters and production profiles remain.

items.title: Cache, object storage, uploads, mail, and notifications
items.description: Add typed cache coordination, bounded streaming storage and uploads, and testable mail and notification contracts with provider adapters.

items.title: React, JSX, components, events, and state
items.description: Checked JSX, TSX generation, typed props, events, and use_state connect to React; lifecycle, broader hooks, accessibility diagnostics, and component-package coverage remain.

items.title: Browser routing, server state, forms, and platform APIs
items.description: Native declaration and Result bridges prove initial router and query integration; typed route generation, form lifecycle, DOM breadth, and browser resource semantics remain.

items.title: Browser assets, bundling, development, and HMR
items.description: Coordinate ordinary bundlers with TypeRB generation, CSS and static assets, code splitting, source maps, stale-chunk recovery, size budgets, and local HMR.

items.title: Shared wire contracts, validation, and compatibility
items.description: Records, enums, newtypes, typed binders, endpoint metadata, and generated clients share a foundation; field validation, schema diff, versioning, and generic contract identity remain.

items.title: External SDK and service integration
items.description: Package-owned shims can normalize narrow SDK calls across modes; credentials, typed service models, pagination, streaming, cancellation, and reusable provider conformance remain.

areas.title: Testing, editors, and learning
areas.description: The feedback loops required to understand, test, edit, and debug TypeRB every day.

items.title: Portable test declarations and runner
items.description: Colocated tests, source-located failures, filtering, JSON events, backend execution, and editor integration exist; the language-level workflow still needs broader application evidence.

items.title: Test lifecycle, assertions, doubles, and determinism
items.description: Core assertions and in-process Web testing exist; setup and teardown, richer diffs, verified doubles, fake time and randomness, and external-call isolation remain.

items.title: Application, component, browser, and end-to-end tests
items.description: Web, ORM, Jobs, and native conformance fixtures cover important slices; browser hosts, component accessibility, Playwright integration, and standard full-stack fixtures remain.

items.title: TypeRB coverage and scalable CI test operation
items.description: Map backend coverage to TypeRB source and add thresholds, affected selection, sharding, retries, flake visibility, and common CI report formats.

items.title: Language-server everyday editing
items.description: Use compiler-backed diagnostics, formatting, completion, hover, signature help, navigation, rename, symbols, selection, folding, highlights, and quick fixes.

items.title: Ecosystem-aware language intelligence
items.description: Project imports and generated ORM declarations participate in completion and navigation; packages, schemas, routes, jobs, contracts, components, and large workspaces need deeper indexing.

items.title: Visual Studio Code integration
items.description: A thin extension supplies syntax, snippets, language-server features, standalone files, Test Explorer integration, and Go debug artifact support without duplicating compiler semantics.

items.title: Neovim, JetBrains, and GitHub integrations
items.description: Use the shared language server and TextMate grammar through a Neovim plugin, LSP4IJ setup, and a GitHub syntax-highlighting extension.

items.title: Cross-target source debugging
items.description: Go debug builds and Delve integration exist; Ruby and TypeScript adapters, target-standard maps, browser and worker process selection, and exception mapping remain.

items.title: REPL, playground, and guided tour
items.description: Explore persistent typed state, completion, formatting, inspection, interrupts, and the same evaluator through local and hosted interactive surfaces.

items.title: Searchable reference, guides, and maintained tutorials
items.description: The hosted documentation covers language, tooling, packages, and application slices; 1.0 needs complete searchable references, upgrade paths, and additional production-shaped tutorials.

areas.title: Distribution, compatibility, and operation
areas.description: Reproducible installation, release, security, deployment, and long-term maintenance boundaries.

items.title: Direct binary, Homebrew, and container distribution
items.description: Install TypeRB directly or with Homebrew and build or run projects through the published container workflow.

items.title: Reproducible CI builds and deployable artifacts
items.description: Frozen package installs and deterministic generated trees provide a base; production bundles, source maps, cache policy, and end-to-end artifact verification remain.

items.title: Supported operating-system, architecture, and toolchain matrix
items.description: Current toolchains and multiple installation paths are tested, while 1.0 needs an explicit supported matrix and complete target-runtime conformance.

items.title: Signed releases, provenance, and SBOMs
items.description: Release automation packages and attests important artifacts; the complete compiler, package, container, and dependency provenance story still needs a public support boundary.

items.title: Compatibility, deprecation, and migration policy
items.description: Define version and upgrade rules independently for language semantics, the standard library, official packages, extension protocols, generated wires, and database contracts.

items.title: Security audit and supply-chain response
items.description: Checksums, secure primitives, typed Web defaults, and bounded extension principles exist; advisories, dependency audit, secret policy, and coordinated response remain.

items.title: Deployment, observability, and failure recovery
items.description: Document and verify health, readiness, telemetry, redaction, schema and queue operations, rollback, and recovery for representative deployed applications.

items.title: Predictable release cadence and support policy
items.description: Publish supported versions, security-update expectations, deprecation windows, release cadence, and lifecycle commitments before 1.0 stability is claimed.
